title: Quake: Adaptive Indexing for Vector Search
problem: Static vector search indexes (HNSW, DiskANN) don't adapt to dynamic workloads with changing update/query patterns, leading to suboptimal performance
motivation: Real-world vector search workloads are highly dynamic (update/query ratios change); adaptive indexing can improve both query and update performance significantly
method: The system splits vectors into multiple partition levels and uses a learned cost model (a machine-learned prediction system that estimates how expensive different index arrangements will be) to continuously monitor how the workload changes—which vectors are being queried, updated, and how often. When access patterns shift, it restructures the index automatically to keep performance high. It also accounts for NUMA locality (the fact that data sits in physically distributed memory banks at different distances from CPU cores), placing frequently accessed data closer to reduce latency.
key_novelty: It learns which access patterns matter most in your workload and restructures the index automatically, with parallelism that respects NUMA locality so parallel tasks access data physically close to the CPU cores executing them.
contributions: Adaptive multi-level partitioning for vector search
Learned cost model for structure selection
4.5-126x update latency improvement on dynamic workloads
limitations: Primarily CPU-focused; GPU acceleration not discussed; cost model generalization to unseen workloads unclear; memory overhead of multi-level partitioning not specified
